doc.title: Doug Carn interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 24, 2023

title: Motherless Child and the organ as a church instrument
summary: Discussing his first record, he says the organ is a church instrument and complains of being held to one bag.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: Well I want to thank you for your time and I want to re-visit — we had had a start to this interview that we had to re-do and I had mentioned the — “Sometimes I Feel Like a Motherless Child” from your very first record.
Yeah Joey DeFrancesca recorded that one too. I was sad that he had to pass away so early.
Yes. Well it’s a beautiful recording and it sounded like, you know, like you were in church.

Well the organ is a church instrument. You know that’s why black people love it so much, you know, certain black people. Certain black people don’t like organ or didn’t like it because they felt that it kept them in that old school church blues idiom and they wanted to go forward you know. I said, “Well you ever heard Larry Young Junior?” They said, “Oh yeah I heard that noise and all that wild stuff.” I said, “Yeah but it’s stuff like ‘Unity’ and that is “Zoltan,” that other ones that he did too.” You know they tried to hold you to one bag when you play jazz you know, but they didn’t hold Van Cliburn in one bag playing classical music. He can play a Rachmaninoff or Debussy you know. Because that’s Van Cliburn. But if you go outside the established perimeters that they’ve got for you then you’ve either sold out or changed you know. They want to see you play until you die on the stage you know. You know ‘til you’re in a wheelchair and ragged and can hardly play you know. And I remember I was in Kansas City and was it Jay McShann was playing — was it Jay McShann that Bird used to play with?
